brief: Combinatorial optimization in geometry (Rivin) — extends and unifies results on ideal polyhedra in H³ to singular Euclidean structures on surfaces, possibly with infinitely many singularities.
extended:
**Combinatorial optimization in geometry 1** — Igor Rivin. arXiv:math/9907032v1 [math.GT], 6 Jul 1999.

Extends and unifies earlier results, generalising the framework of ideal polyhedra in H³ to that of singular Euclidean structures on surfaces, possibly with an infinite number of singularities. The method is variational: geometric structures are characterised as optima of a combinatorial/convex problem.

**Why it may bear here.** A variational characterisation of ideal hyperbolic structures is the same shape as the LP/SDP optimisation this corpus uses for operator selection, and the ideal-polyhedron setting is where hyperbolic volume comes from. Structural resemblance, not an established connection.
